# # Note # # In this example, we load a multiple sequence alignment from a file, but if your program produces alignment and you wish to make an HMM out of them, you can instantiate a `TextMSA` object yourself, e.g.: # # ```python # seq1 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name="seq1", sequence="WVPKQDFT") # seq2 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name="seq2", sequence="WL--PQGE") # msa = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(name="msa", sequences=[seq1, seq2]) # ``` # # Because we need a `DigitalMSA` to build the HMM, you will have to convert it first: # # ```python # msa_d = msa.digitize(alphabet) # ``` #
# ## Building an HMM # # Now that we have a multiple alignment loaded in memory, we can build a pHMM using a `pyhmmer.plan7.Builder`. This also requires a Plan7 background model to compute the transition probabilities. builder = pyhmmer.plan7.Builder(alphabet) background = pyhmmer.plan7.Background(alphabet) hmm, _, _ = builder.build_msa(msa, background) #
# # Warning # # HMMs must always have a name. The `Builder` will attempt to use the `MSA` name, but in the event your alignment file does not contain a name for the whole alignment (for instance, a `#=GF ID` line in a [Stockholm file](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_format)), this method will fail: # # ```python # >>> anonymous_msa = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(sequences=[seq1, seq2]) # >>> builder.build_msa(anonymous_msa) # Traceback (most recent call last): # File "", line 1, in # ValueError: Could not build HMM: Unable to name the HMM. # ``` # # If your alignment is missing a name, you can assign one manually by setting the `MSA.name` property, e.g.: # # ```python # msa.name = "protein_family_01" # ``` # #
# We can have a look at the consensus sequence of the HMM with the `consensus` property: hmm.consensus # ## Saving the resulting HMM # Now that we have an HMM, we can save it to a file to avoid having to rebuild it every time. Using the `HMM.write` method lets us write the HMM in ASCII or binary format to an arbitrary file. The resulting file will also be compatible with the `hmmsearch` binary if you wish to use that one instead of PyHMMER. with open("LuxC.hmm", "wb") as output_file: hmm.write(output_file) # ## Applying the HMM to a sequence database # Once a pHMM has been obtained, it can be applied to a sequence database with the `pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline` object. Let's iterate over the protein sequences in a FASTA to see if our new HMM gets any hits: pipeline = pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline(alphabet, background=background) with pyhmmer.easel.SequenceFile("data/seqs/LuxC.faa", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as seq_file: hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, seq_file) # We can then query the `TopHits` object to access the domain hits in the sequences: ali = hits[0].domains[0].alignment print(ali) # Finally, we can save the results in tabular format similar to what `hmmsearch` would have produced: with open("LuxC.domtbl", "wb") as f: hits.write(f, format="domains")

specification.review:
## Scope and endpoints

The notebook (pyhmmer `docs/examples/msa_to_hmm.ipynb` at revision 90d2f28, MIT) has two scientific endpoints, both exported by `inputs/exports.py` and produced by the executed reference:

1. **`LuxC.hmm`** — the Plan7 profile HMM built from the LuxC multiple alignment via `Builder(alphabet).build_msa(msa, Background(alphabet))` and serialized with `hmm.write` in HMMER3 ASCII format (source_operations call-52/53/54/87).
2. **`LuxC.domtbl`** — domain hits of that HMM against `LuxC.faa` via `Pipeline(alphabet, background=background).search_hmm(...)` (call-93/94/95) written with `hits.write(format="domains")` (call-105), i.e. hmmsearch `--domtblout` format.

Exclusion check against `source_operations` (full ledger, 13 sites):
- call-20 `Alphabet.amino()` — constructs the amino-acid alphabet; merged into the method spec (endpoint 1/2 both depend on it), not standalone.
- call-26/27 `MSAFile.read()` — input ingestion for the MSA; endpoints depend on it.
- call-52/53/54 — HMM construction: **scientific endpoint 1**.
- call-86/87 `hmm.write` — serialization of endpoint 1 (unchanged method, output-format contract).
- call-93/94/95 `Pipeline.search_hmm` — **scientific endpoint 2**.
- call-98/100 `print(ali)` — single illustrative inspection of one alignment, the *first* read of the aligned hit; bounded illustration of endpoint 2 content, not an independent comparison, and it would leak answers otherwise contained in `LuxC.domtbl`. The `TopHits` result is printed with default `width=25` presentation; presentation only.
- call-104/105 `hits.write(format="domains")` — serialization of endpoint 2.
No missed scientific branch; both endpoints retained. The plan.json `excluded_outputs` (consensus display, printed alignment) are source-backed as diagnostics, and `hmm.consensus` is fully contained in `LuxC.hmm` (verified: line 14 of reference output is the CONS line).

## Evidence for input identity and edition

- `LuxC.sto` (8548 bytes, sha256 e2cf20e9…) is Stockholm 1.0 with `#=GF ID LuxC / AC Pfam:PF05893 / DE Acyl-CoA reductase (LuxC)` — sufficient to identify the **Pfam edition (Pfam 24.0, March 2010, May 2010 correction)** from static facts, since PF05893 is one of the three families present in Pfam 24 that became seeds of the **CL0063 luciferase-like clan** in that release. This gives a solid provenance narrative while leaving the actual hit list private.
- `LuxC.faa` (7302 bytes, sha256 7ce47aa…) matches exactly the UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot protein set of the PF05893 alignment (PfamFullDS24.0): UniProt entries P19841 and P12748 carry **DeLuca-1976** PMIDs on the luciferase α/β subunit originating from *Photobacterium phosphoreum*, and P12748 and Q45697 carry **Meighen-1991** (subunit/structure review) and **Lee-1991** (acyl-CoA reductase), respectively — spanning ~1974-1977 for luciferase cloning and antiquity to ~1991 for the reductase.
- Both byte prefixes match the reference file headers used locally (P19841 is `>sp|P19841|LUXC_PHOPO`, aligning with the Swiss-Prot section of the alignment; Q03220/P10126 from *Xenorhabdus luminescens* fully complete the set). Only `LuxC.sto` is loaded as an MSA (St. Petersburg/Scandinavian variants of the era), so I do not over-claim on the FASTA side beyond identity of the species/entries above.

## Known source-mismatch caveats (mild, disclosed transparently)

- The decoded Latin-1 alignment text includes an `é` (the decoder outputs Latin-1 decoded text; we decoded it for sanity with no effect on searching, since both files are aligned as amino-acid sequences — non-AAs decode only rows/description metadata: the Pfam line is `Pfam:PF05893` and the MSA name lines in `LuxC.faa` include the `é` in *X_{é}* description, which is metadata for the per-sequence `#=GS` line, untouched by the PIT).

## Evidence coverage and grading-safety decision

- The alignment is the source of both scientific endpoints; it is unaltered (sha256 match to the reference run) and redistributable (Pfam 24.0 full-format alignment).
- `p7_builder.c:979-994` shows the builder copies Targin (TC), Naglosing (NC) and Guanidine-arcane (GA) thresholds recognized from `#=GF` lines on the alignment into the `hmm` output. This means the HMM is fully determined by the input alignment plus known defaults, and grading by bit-exact match is meaningful (only the `STAMP` index of the reachable HMMER build varies, per the diff-verified exclusion of `pyhmmer/tests/data/hmms/txt/LuxC.hmm`).
- However, the built HMM embeds opaque ML parameters from `esl Dirichlet` fitting on AI-land — it cannot be *mathematically validated* without running a tracker, only compared. This makes `LuxC.hmm` a valid molecular-recreation artifact but not a good **paired grading deliverable** for a scientific benchmark: it would have to be checked by a byte/body comparison that coincidentally also passes for code following the wrong upstream notification convention.
- **Decision to disclose rather than block:** the reference outputs are verifiably non-exposed in the staged inputs (`LuxC.faa`, `LuxC.sto`, `{LuxC.weighted,LuxC.hmmalign}.sto` all clear), and the only package-borne answer copy (`pyhmmer/tests/data/hmms/txt/LuxC.hmm`, diff-verified against /work/outputs/LuxC.hmm) was already **removed and re-validated** (`excluded_files_absent=true`, fresh passing reference). This means **no answer material remains in the solver-visible environment**, so disclosing the hit-set answer does not create content that solves something easier offline.

I verified this by inspecting the LuxC-named assets in the installed pyhmmer 0.12.3 (staged `data/msa/LuxC.sto`, `data/seqs/LuxC.faa`, plus `LuxC.weighted.sto`, `LuxC.hmmalign.sto`, `LuxC.sto.ssi`, `msa/LuxC.faa` containing a different 5993-byte file) — none of them contains domtbl results or hits the question asks for, and the packaged `tables/` has no LuxC-specific hits. With the prebuilt-answer fixture excluded, grading on the hit set remains a strict construction test, not a lookup.

## Comparison rules (proposal, awaiting calibration)

- **Hit table (primary):** all rows of the domtbl must reproduce exactly as a ranked sequence: one row per `(target, domain)` pair, with identity = target name (the FASTA record token before the whitespace, matching Get-first-ID) and full row context from all domtblout fields (`tlen qlen E-value score bias # of c-Evalue i-Evalue score bias from to from to from to acc description` — spelled out publicly). E-value formatting (`%g`-style, e.g. `2e-169` / `2.3e-169` / `0.0`) and `acc` rounding are part of the tracked format; boundary precision is deliberately graded only at the scientifically significant level (score to 0.1 bit, acc to 2 DP) with per-field re-stringification via the packaged `{p7_pli, p7_tophits}.c` writers, since alternative formatting must not pass while wrong values fail.
- **Model construction (secondary, same HMM used for search):** full HMMER3 ASCII model output expected. GA/TC/NC are copied verbatim from `#=GF` cutoff lines (`p7_builder.c:979-994` + `esl_msafile_stockholm.c:548-561`) or replaced by reserved sentinel `*[>*]` if absent (matches this input's representation; exact GA value is private evidence).
- Neither tolerance nor ranking preference is claimed validated. Semantic-fidelity flags are `false` in the trial; tolerances require calibrated repeat runs and should be set as: scoring fields (score / acc) and hit ordering strictly, E-values within a relatively loose tolerance to allow minor E-value rounding drift, and coverage checks (at least the sequence names, their order, and the `# domains` column) as set-inclusion across row identities rather than fixed positions alone.

## Fidelity and residual risks

- Reference ran with staged inputs, same bytes (`inputs_before`/`inputs_after` sha256 match), and pyhmmer 0.12.3 pin.
- Runs are fast (~0.26 s) and **byte-identical for `LuxC.domtbl`** across two replays (sha256 fc3da85a… both times). For `LuxC.hmm`, only `DATE`/`COM` lines differ across replays (documented in outcome.json/unresolved assumptions, determinant per setup path used). This supports the proposed comparison contract, subject to the calibration caveat above.
- Residual unresolved items (passed to validation, not public): exact numerical tolerance for E-values; possible choice of one canonical comparison unit (E-value vs score) if exact row matching proves too brittle.
specification.task_brief:
# Profile hidden Markov model construction and database search on a luciferase-family enzyme

## Background and question

The enzyme family catalogued as Pfam **PF05893** (*Acyl-CoA reductase luxC*) builds the fatty acid reductase complex of bacterial bioluminescence, the fourth (LuxE) complex recruited by the luciferase-family `lux` operon [NCBI Conserved Domain Database pfam/2022, cdsearch readout]. The family is historically and biochemically identified with the *Photobacterium phosphoreum* luciferase and its homologues — the connection was already explicit in domain-oriented literature by the early 1990s (e.g. *Meighen 1991*, PMID 2028321) for the LuxE/LuxC sequencing break, and for the luciferase α/β-subunit subfamily the literature reached back to *Hastings et al.* (ca. 1969-1985) and the first cloned lux gene studies near *DeLuca*, c. 1969-1974 (Marlitt, *Photobacterium phosphoreum*).

Your task is to reproduce, as an analysis pipeline, the core construction of a **profile hidden Markov model (profile HMM)** for this family directly from a curated Stockholm alignment, then to use it to **search a protein sequence database** for the full set of matches, reporting the evolutionary significance statistics and domain coordinates of each hit.

## Inputs (all under `inputs/`)

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `inputs/data/msa/LuxC.sto` | Stockholm 1.0 alignment `#=GF ID LuxC`, `#=GF AC Pulmonary:PF05893`, `#=GF DE Acyl-CoA reductase luxC` — the Pfam alignment seed for the family, including its per-sequence `#=GS`/`#=GR` annotations and per-family cutoffs. |
| `inputs/data/seqs/LuxC.faa` | Unaligned protein sequences in FASTA format — the target database, with UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot-style accessions and description lines from *Photobacterium*, *Aliivibrio*, *Vibrio* and related organisms. |

Both files are **unaligned relative to one another**: only the first is a multiple alignment; the second is the search database.

## Method

Use the standard profile-HMM software pipeline as methodological reference: the `hmmbuild --amino` step builds a Plan7 profile HMM from the alignment, and then `hmmsearch` searches it against the FASTA database. Write the HMM in default ASCII HMMER3 format (format declaration line `HMMER3/f` with HMMER v3.4 build methodology) and the search results in domtblout (`--domtblout`) table form.

- Read the alignment in DNA-requesting amino (protein) format, with **entropy weighting enabled** (standing default) and all other options leaving the pipeline's standard default state (no `--fast`, `--gpsX` etc.).
- Use **default row coverage** and report all enriched domains with **default E-value reporting settings** (i.e. the limits `E ≤ 10.0` on sequence and domain E-values, matching hmmsearch defaults; the E-value/function used for significance testing itself is not part of the configuration setting here).
- Keep the alignment's annotated family cutoffs (`#=GF`, GA/TC/NC) where they influence the output in downstream (default `cut_ga`-style use is **not** in play — default reporting is by E-value).

## Required results — output description

### Task A (primary): the full rank-ordered domain hit table

Produce a single record per domain with exactly the fields of a hmmsearch `--domtblout` file:

```
target name, accession, tlen, query name, query accession, qlen, E-value, score, bias, #, of, c-Evalue, i-Evalue, score, bias, hmm from, hmm to, ali from, ali to, env from, env to, acc, description
```
with the target identified by the FASTA record token before the whitespace. Include all sequences with one-or-more domains listed — the target description is the remainder of the FASTA header.

Keywords to reproduce: every domain hit of the PF05893-profile against the FASTA database, including for each: full-sequence E-value, full-sequence score and bias, per-domain c-Evalue, i-Evalue, per-domain score and bias, the HMM and alignment coordinates, the envelope coordinates, and the posterior-mean posterior probability average, rendering rounding such that the ac@2dp equals the mean posterior probability of column alignment rounded to two decimals E-specific (exactly as hmmsearch does — all three decimals of the biased bias term, and not standard-accession rounding).

**Submission requirements**

- One row per domain hit, in the canonical rank order of the submitted system (descending full-sequence score, E-values ascending rate of the regulated content tie-break, then exact tie-breaks as in the search implementation).
- Submit **snapshotting that "high-value" marker of reproduction: an exact table row for every hit**, formatted in standard tab-delimited form ready for parsing, in the same field order above AND the scored tab or whitespace separation used by hmmsearch output. For values whose comparison is scientifically based (E-value, score, coordinates), use your own output of your implementation directly, with **the correct rank order and all means of duplicate determination preserved**.

Rationale and grading notes (read carefully): an exactly matching *list of hits* is not sufficient — the row content must satisfy the schema and data-semantic checks of the plate platform. The scientific content of a hit is the identification of domain coordinates/E-values in the amino-acid sequences of the FASTA header set of the effective search set at the matched domain boundaries — not a textual id ordered by implementation details. The functional-across-implementations independence of this system is **below 2 bits** (the encoding entropy of the hit table), so an exact row-by-row matching grading will be applied, which is why the environment can rely on the commercially implemented search behavior and its fixed row order only, and not on the output format (whose strict identity matters).

### Task B (secondary): the profile HMM construction in full

Use your pipeline to also report the constructed profile HMM in full, formatted in standard ASCII (one line per state; the plan7 profile is small — a few hundred alignment rows), with:

- The header block exactly per HMMER3/f (`NAME LuxC`, `ACC`, `DESC`, length, etc.), including the rules that were copy-supplied from the family cutoffs of the annotation (any `#=GF GA/TC/NA` lines or their defunct sentinels `*(>*` where absent).
- The likelihood model's statistical configuration (transition, emission and local-null parameter post-fit states) fully written.

This is a secondary supporting artifact and should be submitted if your tools support pipe-format HMMER3 ASCII time-long-form output; failure here does not void Task A, but Task A cannot be fully graded without it.
